```
(Currently Amended) Claim 1: A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

(Currently Amended) Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, without requiring the pump to idle when connected to atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) Claim 3: The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, without requiring the directional control valve to be fully closed.

(Currently Amended) Claim 4: The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

(Currently Amended) Claim 5: The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) Claim 7: The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

(Currently Amended) Claim 8: A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, without requiring the pump to idle when connected to atmosphere, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

(Currently Amended) Claim 9: The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, without requiring the directional control valve to be fully closed.

(Currently Amended) Claim 11: The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) Claim 13: The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

(Currently Amended) Claim 14: A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, but not identifying the engine type as internal combustion.

(Currently Amended) Claim 15: The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, while excluding restrictions on the functionality of the valve.

(Currently Amended) Claim 19: The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.
```
